name: Ligolo-ng
what: A tunneling tool for authorized network pivoting. Instead of a simple SOCKS proxy it brings up a TUN interface so you can route IP traffic into a compromised or jump network with multiple concurrent tunnels.
when: During an internal or assumed-breach engagement when you have a foothold agent on an approved host and need to reach otherwise inaccessible segments without dropping a heavyweight C2 solely for routing.
example: Download matching proxy and agent binaries from the Ligolo-ng GitHub releases for your platforms.
Start the proxy on the assessment host, create a TUN interface as documented, and run the agent on the approved foothold.
Add routes only for in-scope subnets, then continue scanning or administration through the tunnel.
Close tunnels and remove routes when that phase of the test ends.
pitfalls: The project is explicitly for authorized network penetration tests; unauthorized pivoting is illegal.
TUN setup needs privileges on the proxy host; practice in a lab before the engagement.
Tunnel traffic still needs to match the rules of engagement and any geo or segmentation constraints.
